newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen futures up slightly on JGB strength.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen futures up slightly on JGB strength.

text.p: Key December three-month euroyen deposit rate futures ended Friday's TIFFE day session slightly higher, in line with a rise in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures.
December settled at 99.14, after trading between 99.11 and 99.14. Turnover on the day was 45,586 lots.
A fall in Tokyo stocks also helped to underpin euroyen futures, traders said.
If December breaches resistance at 99.15, it could climb to 99.20, a brokerage house trader said.
"The support at 99.10 is becoming more solid now," she said.
Market participants were cautious about testing the upside ahead of Friday's release of U.S. employment data for March, traders said.
"Stronger-than-expected non-farm payrolls data could have a big negative impact on the U.S. markets, so we need to see the data before making our next move," a city bank trader said.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said in Tokyo on Friday that it was important for Japan to open its markets further and promote domestic demand-led growth.
Traders said Rubin's remarks had little impact on the euroyen futures market as he did not say what specific actions Japan should take to achieve domestic-led growth.
The BOJ drained 400 billion yen from the money market on Friday morning, leaving a surplus of nearly 100 billion yen.
Key unsecured overnight call money was mostly traded at 0.48 percent, flat from Thursday's weighted average.
"Upward pressure on the overnight rate has eased as more banks begin to raise longer-term funds through such instruments as certificates of deposit," said a city bank trader.
About 20 billion yen worth of three-month CDs was issued at 0.55 percent, unchanged from Thursday.
About 10 billion yen worth of one-month CDs was issued at 0.53 percent, down from 0.54 percent on Thursday.
Two-month CDs were offered at 0.54 percent.
